### Waking Is Not the Same as Being Ready

Opening your eyes before the alarm does not mean your brain is fully ready for work. Research links abrupt waking from deep N3 sleep with stronger sleep inertia than waking from lighter N2 sleep, while REM falls between them. In a 34-person nap study, N3 waking also showed related brain-function differences.

### A Broad Hormone Transition

In a 2025 home study of 201 adults, free cortisol began rising, on average, 187 minutes before waking and peaked 36 minutes afterward. Its rise did not speed up sharply at the waking boundary. A separate study of 16 men found a marked ACTH-and-cortisol increase after waking, suggesting preparation unfolds across phases, not as a minute-perfect countdown.

## In one line

A pre-alarm awakening may be genuine without being perfectly timed: the body can approach wakefulness while the mind and body are still catching up.
